rules.title: Entity Props Pattern
rules.description: Entities MUST encapsulate constructor arguments inside a dedicated Props object to keep signatures stable and explicit.

goodExamples.caption: Entity constructor receives a single props object.

badExamples.caption: Long positional constructor arguments are fragile and error-prone.

rules.title: No Logic in DTOs
rules.description: DTOs MUST remain pure data contracts. Validation and business rules belong to Value Objects, Entities, and Use Cases.

goodExamples.caption: DTO remains a pure shape declaration.

badExamples.caption: Behavior in DTOs creates hidden domain logic in the wrong layer.

rules.title: Layer Isolation
rules.description: Domain and application layers MUST not directly depend on infrastructure details such as Prisma clients or HTTP adapters.

goodExamples.caption: Use case depends on abstraction, not infrastructure.

badExamples.caption: Application layer is tightly coupled to persistence implementation.

rules.title: Value Object Collections
rules.description: Collections in aggregates MUST use Value Objects for normalization and invariants instead of passing primitive strings directly.

goodExamples.caption: RuleTag enforces normalization for every collection entry.

badExamples.caption: Primitive collection bypasses normalization and duplicate checks.

rules.title: Factory Method Pattern
rules.description: Aggregates MUST expose static factory methods and hide constructors to guarantee invariant validation at creation time.

goodExamples.caption: Factory method centralizes creation and validation flow.

badExamples.caption: Public constructor allows bypassing validation and lifecycle controls.
